symbols.name: rho_i
symbols.meaning: density of ice (taken constant, see A4)

symbols.name: rho_v
symbols.meaning: mass concentration of water vapor in the gas

symbols.name: c_v(T)
symbols.meaning: specific heat of water vapor at constant pressure, dh_v/dT

symbols.name: H
symbols.meaning: enthalpy per unit volume of the ice-gas mixture

symbols.name: J_v
symbols.meaning: diffusive mass flux of water vapor

symbols.name: m_dot
symbols.meaning: mass of vapor deposited as ice per unit volume and time (negative for sublimation)

symbols.name: k(phi, T)
symbols.meaning: effective thermal conductivity of the ice-gas mixture

symbols.name: C(phi, T)
symbols.meaning: volumetric heat capacity of the mixture, phi rho_i c_i + (1-phi) rho_v c_v (+ air if present)

symbols.name: L(T)

steps.title: Integral energy balance
steps.why: Conservation of energy for any fixed control volume $V$ in the pore space. Pressure is taken as uniform, so the stored energy is the enthalpy $H$. Energy enters through the conductive flux $\mathbf q$ and the enthalpy carried by diffusing vapor, $h_v\mathbf J_v$.
steps.operation: first law for a fixed control volume at constant pressure
steps.latex: \frac{d}{dt}\int_V H\,dV = -\oint_{\partial V}\left(\mathbf q + h_v\mathbf J_v\right)\cdot\mathbf n\,dA

steps.title: Local energy balance
steps.why: $V$ is arbitrary and the fields are smooth (A1), so applying the divergence theorem gives a pointwise equation.

steps.title: Mass balances of ice and vapor
steps.why: Ice is immobile and gains mass $\dot m$ by deposition. The vapor loses the same mass. With constant ice density (A4), the ice balance links $\dot m$ to $\partial_t\phi$.
steps.operation: mass conservation for each water phase

steps.title: Mixture enthalpy
steps.why: The phase field sets the volume fractions, so the enthalpy per volume is the fraction-weighted sum of the ice and vapor enthalpies.

steps.title: Time derivative of H
steps.operation: differentiate S4 in t (product and chain rule)
steps.latex: \partial_t H = h_i\rho_i\partial_t\phi + \phi\rho_i c_i\partial_t T + h_v\partial_t\left[(1-\phi)\rho_v\right] + (1-\phi)\rho_v c_v\partial_t T

steps.title: Eliminate vapor storage
steps.why:
Substitute the vapor balance from S3 for $\partial_t[(1-\phi)ho_v]$, and expand $
abla\cdot(h_v\mathbf J_v)=h_v
abla\cdot\mathbf J_v + c_v\mathbf J_v\cdot
abla T$. The $h_v
abla\cdot\mathbf J_v$ terms cancel.
steps.operation: substitution of S3 and S5 into S2
steps.latex: \left[\phi\rho_i c_i + (1-\phi)\rho_v c_v\right]\partial_t T - (h_v-h_i)\rho_i\partial_t\phi + c_v\mathbf J_v\cdot\nabla T + \nabla\cdot\mathbf q = 0

steps.title: Fourier law, latent heat, neglect vapor enthalpy advection
steps.why: Introduce $\mathbf q=-k(\phi,T)\nabla T$ (A5), $C(\phi,T)=\phi\rho_i c_i+(1-\phi)\rho_v c_v$, and $L(T)=h_v-h_i$. Drop $c_v\mathbf J_v\cdot\nabla T$: its ratio to conduction is about $10^{-8}$ or less (see neglected).
steps.operation: substitution of constitutive law and definitions; drop small term

steps.title: Residual in 3D Cartesian form
steps.why: Write the divergence in Cartesian components and move every term to one side. Units: every term is in W m^-3.
steps.operation: expand divergence in x, y, z; collect as R
steps.latex: R = C\,\partial_t T - \partial_x(k\,\partial_x T) - \partial_y(k\,\partial_y T) - \partial_z(k\,\partial_z T) - \rho_i L\,\partial_t\phi = 0

check.printed: no tools in this run (units by hand: J m^-3 K^-1 * K s^-1 = W m^-3; W m^-1 K^-1 * K m^-2 = W m^-3; kg m^-3 * J kg^-1 * s^-1 = W m^-3)

assumptions_used: A1: $\phi(x,y,z,t)$ is a known, smooth field (given), and $T$ is smooth.
A2: The pressure is uniform and constant, and the system is at rest, so the energy content is the enthalpy. Pressure work, viscous dissipation and kinetic energy are dropped.
A3: The pore space holds only ice (fraction $\phi$) and gas (fraction $1-\phi$). Ice and gas share one local temperature $T$, and the ice is immobile.
A4: The ice density $\rho_i$ is constant (needed in S3 to write $\dot m=\rho_i\partial_t\phi$).
A5: Heat conduction follows Fourier's law with an isotropic effective conductivity $k(\phi,T)$.
A6: Enthalpy advection by vapor diffusion, $c_v\mathbf J_v\cdot\nabla T$, is negligible compared with conduction.

neglected.effect: Enthalpy carried by vapor diffusion, $c_v\mathbf J_v\cdot\nabla T$
neglected.why: $\mathbf J_v\sim D\nabla\rho_v$ with $\rho_v\sim10^{-6}$ kg m^-3 near 200 K. The ratio to conduction is about $c_v D\rho_v/(k\ell)\cdot\ell \sim 1850\cdot10^{-4}\cdot10^{-6}/2.5\sim10^{-7}$, and its gradient factor makes it smaller still.

neglected.effect: Gas convection (bulk flow of the gas in the pores)
neglected.why: The pores are small (tens of micrometers) and the pressures are low, so the Peclet number is far below 1.
Pressure changes are tiny compared with $\rho c T$, and the flow is negligible.
With pore size $d\sim10^{-4}$ m, $4\sigma T^3 d\sim2\times10^{-4}$ W m^-1 K^-1, much less than $k$ of ice ($\sim2.5$).

neglected.effect: Interfacial (surface) energy and Gibbs-Thomson change of $L$
neglected.why: $\gamma/(\rho_i L r)\sim0.1/(920\cdot2.8\times10^6\cdot10^{-6})\sim4\times10^{-5}$ relative to the latent heat.
The relative change is about $10^{-4}$ per 1 K, a negligible correction to $\rho_i\partial_t\phi$.

neglected.effect: Non-equilibrium between ice and gas temperatures
neglected.why: The thermal diffusion time across a pore, about $d^2/\alpha\sim10^{-8}/10^{-6}=10^{-2}$ s, is far shorter than sublimation time scales.
